story_review.one_viewing_summary: This is the planned A chain, not observed pixels. A flooding San Antonio yard reaches the fence post's ankle mark before the phone's late warning. The prototype station charges from the sun, needs no tower and watches the water with four lenses that light as it rises. Its own chip lights an amber risk lamp without reaching a server, and its radio carries to a hub, where a responder reads a spreading flood map. On a curb notice board the corrected detail shot keeps the whole 98.82% card, heading and assessments tag in frame while a blank field result card slides in. The following shot then pushes that card off the left edge to '2%' while a stamp prints none reported, before a finger reads a blank map and a technician latches the plan into the prototype's case.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The film opens on whether a station can judge rising street water with no power line or cell tower. It answers yes as a disclosed design through charge, sensing, on-chip judgment, radio and the hub map, and it ends on the plan kept with an uninstalled prototype, so no deployment outcome is invented. The answer is weakened at the limit: the reported validation figure that s7 now shows whole is cut to a misleading '2%' in s8-shot-1, exactly where the narration says no field result exists.
story_review.weakest_transition: The s7 to s8 cut at 49.2 s is the weakest. The cut from the corrected detail view to the two-card view keeps the same card readable at first. Within about 0.4 s, though, the s8-shot-1 push slides that card off the left edge, so the bridge of the same card beside a blank result card breaks into a truncated figure.
